html:
The Nyvukagmit, or Naukan Yupik, were the people of Naukan, a village on Cape Dezhnev at the eastern tip of Asia, facing Alaska across the Bering Strait. They spoke Naukan Yupik, a Yupik language.

They hunted walrus, seals and whales from skin boats, and traded and married across the strait with the Iñupiat of Alaska and with their Chukchi neighbours on land. Their way of life came from the Thule tradition of Arctic sea hunters.

The Russian explorer Semyon Dezhnev sailed round the cape in 1648. In 1958 the Soviet government closed Naukan and moved its people to other villages in Chukotka. Only a few dozen people still speak the language. Related groups include the Chaplino Yupik.
